frontMatter.introduction:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual has been developed to establish a structured framework for the effective management, control, and continual improvement of operations within Integrated Merchandising Solutions LLC (IMS).

The manual serves as a comprehensive reference document that outlines the Company's policies, procedures, operational controls, responsibilities, and management practices to ensure consistent service delivery, regulatory compliance, ethical business conduct, employee well-being, information security, environmental responsibility, and sustainable business performance.

The purpose of this manual is to:
Standardize operational processes across all departments and functions.
Define roles, responsibilities, and authorities for effective process management.
Ensure compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, customer, and stakeholder requirements.
Support risk-based thinking and proactive management of operational, environmental, social, ethical, and information security risks.
Promote continual improvement, operational excellence, and sustainable business practices.
Provide guidance for employees, contractors, suppliers, and other relevant stakeholders regarding company procedures and expectations.

frontMatter.scope:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual applies to all business operations, facilities, employees, contractors, temporary personnel, consultants, suppliers, and service providers operating under the management and control of IMS.

The requirements established within this manual apply to all activities associated with corporate management, fulfilment operations, warehousing and distribution, customer support, workforce management, procurement, information management, administrative functions, and other supporting business processes conducted by IMS.

This manual establishes requirements for governance, ethical business conduct, occupational health and safety, environmental management, information security, Talent Development, operational excellence, supplier management, customer service, risk management, regulatory compliance, business continuity, and continual improvement activities.

All personnel working for or on behalf of IMS are required to comply with the requirements outlined in this SOP Manual and all associated policies, procedures, standards, and work instructions.

sops.title: Data Protection and Information Management Procedure

blocks.text: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes the requirements and processes for protecting IMS information assets, preventing unauthorized access, safeguarding confidential and personal information, and ensuring the effective management of information security incidents. The procedure aims to maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information while supporting business continuity, client trust, and regulatory compliance.
This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporary staff, vendors, and third parties who access, process, store, transmit, or manage information on behalf of IMS.
The procedure applies to:

Client information and business records.
Consumer and campaign-related information.
Employee and contractor information.
Vendor and supplier information.
Laptops, desktops, mobile devices, and removable media.
Corporate networks and communication systems.
Cloud-based applications and storage platforms.
Physical and electronic information assets.

responsibilities: Provide oversight for information security activities.
Review significant information security risks and incidents.
Approve major corrective actions and remediation activities.
Allocate resources necessary to maintain information security controls.
Implement and maintain information security controls.
Conduct periodic reviews of security controls.
Ensure employees comply with information security requirements.
Approve access requests within their departments.
Report actual or suspected incidents immediately.
Protect IMS information accessed during service delivery.
Report security incidents affecting IMS information within 24 hours of discovery.

body.text: All information assets shall be identified and protected according to their business importance and sensitivity.
Examples include:

Client contracts.
Campaign reports.
Operational records.
Employee records.
Financial information.
Supplier information.
Access shall be granted based on business need and approved by the relevant Department Manager.
IMS shall:

Assign unique user IDs.
Restrict access according to job responsibilities.
Review user access rights at least annually.
Remove access within 24 hours of employee termination.
Passwords shall:

Contain a minimum of 12 characters.
Include uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters.
Not be shared with other individuals.
Be changed immediately if compromise is suspected.
MFA shall be enabled for:

Email systems.
Cloud platforms.
Remote access connections.
Administrative accounts.
All company-issued devices shall:

Have antivirus protection installed.
Receive security updates regularly.
Use screen lock protection.
Be encrypted where feasible.
Lost or stolen devices shall be reported within 1 hour of discovery.
Prior to granting access to IMS information:

Appropriate confidentiality agreements shall be executed.
Security requirements shall be communicated.
Access permissions shall be documented and approved.
All personnel shall report suspected or confirmed incidents immediately and no later than 30 minutes after discovery.
Reportable incidents include:

Unauthorized access attempts.
Data breaches.
Malware infections.
Phishing attacks.
Lost or stolen devices.
Unauthorized disclosure of information.
System compromise.
Incident reports shall include:

Date and time.
Description.
Affected assets.
Immediate actions taken.
Containment measures may include:

Isolating affected systems.
Blocking user accounts.
Disconnecting devices from the network.
Restricting access to information.
The Incident Response Team shall initiate investigations:

Critical Incidents – Within 24 Hours.
High Incidents – Within 2 Business Days.
Medium Incidents – Within 5 Business Days.
Investigation records shall include:

Incident details.
Root cause analysis.
Business impact assessment.
Corrective actions.
Recovery activities may include:

Restoring information from backups.
Rebuilding systems.
Password resets.
Security patch implementation.
System validation testing.
Critical systems should be restored within 24 hours where feasible.

rows: Senior Management, IT Security Manager, Department Head
IT Security Manager and Department Head

body.text: Post-incident reviews shall be completed:

Within 10 Business Days for Critical incidents.
Within 20 Business Days for High incidents.
Lessons learned and corrective actions shall be documented.
Information shall only be collected for legitimate business purposes and in accordance with contractual, legal, and operational requirements.

Information shall be stored in approved systems with appropriate security controls.

Sensitive information shall not be stored on personal devices without authorization.
Information may only be shared:

For approved business purposes.
With authorized individuals.
Under applicable confidentiality requirements.
Information shall be securely destroyed when retention requirements expire through:

Secure deletion.
Permanent electronic wiping.
Shredding of physical records.

narrative.text: The IT Security Manager shall conduct:

Quarterly reviews of access rights.
Quarterly vulnerability assessments.
Annual review of information security controls.
Ongoing monitoring of reported incidents.
Management shall receive a security performance summary at least annually.

Within 30 days of joining IMS.
Annually thereafter.
Training topics shall include:

Password security.

Data protection requirements.

Training records shall be maintained for a minimum of 3 years.
Following incident reviews, audits, or assessments, IMS shall implement appropriate corrective and preventive actions, including:

Security control improvements.
Policy revisions.
Infrastructure upgrades.
Additional monitoring measures.

Corrective actions shall be tracked until closure.

sops.title: Key Transaction Approval and Delegation of Authority Procedure

blocks.text: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the governance framework for authorization and approval of key business transactions at IMS.

The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that financial commitments, contractual obligations, procurement activities, client-related expenditures, and operational decisions are reviewed and approved by appropriate authorized personnel before execution.
This procedure aims to:

Prevent unauthorized financial and business commitments.
Establish clear accountability for transaction approvals.
Ensure responsible utilization of IMS resources.
Maintain transparency and traceability of business decisions.
Support effective financial and operational governance.
This SOP applies to all IMS employees, managers, functional leaders, and authorized representatives involved in initiating, reviewing, approving, processing, or recording business transactions.
The procedure covers:

Client project and campaign expenditures.
Procurement of goods and services.
Supplier and vendor commitments.
Purchase orders and service agreements.
Employee expenses and reimbursements.
Capital expenditure.
Contracts and commercial agreements.

sops.title: ESG Due Diligence and Responsible Third-Party Management

blocks.text: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes the framework for Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG), Ethics, Compliance, and Anti-Corruption Due Diligence for third-party management at Integrated Merchandising Solutions LLC (IMS).

As a marketing execution, retail merchandising, retail audit, project management, logistics, warehousing, technology, and field services organization, IMS engages various third parties including staffing agencies, merchandising contractors, logistics providers, warehousing partners, technology vendors, promotional material suppliers, printing vendors, consultants, and service providers.

This procedure ensures that all third-party engagements are evaluated and managed in accordance with IMS's sustainability commitments, ethical standards, anti-corruption requirements, legal obligations, client expectations, information security requirements, and responsible business practices.
The objectives of this SOP are to:

Identify, assess, and mitigate ESG, ethics, compliance, and corruption-related risks associated with third parties.
Promote ethical, socially responsible, and environmentally sustainable business practices throughout the value chain.
Prevent child labour, forced labour, discrimination, bribery, corruption, fraud, conflicts of interest, and other unethical conduct within third-party relationships.
Integrate ESG, ethics, compliance, information security, and anti-corruption considerations into supplier selection, onboarding, evaluation, monitoring, and renewal processes.
Establish a risk-based due diligence process for third-party screening, approval, and ongoing monitoring.
Improve transparency, accountability, and sustainability performance throughout the supply chain and service network.
Support compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and client requirements.
Promote continuous improvement in responsible sourcing and third-party risk management practices.
This SOP applies to:

Employees involved in supplier selection, procurement, vendor management, operations, compliance, sustainability, information security, and contract management.
Suppliers and vendors.
Contractors and subcontractors.
Staffing and manpower agencies.
Logistics and warehousing providers.
Technology and software vendors.
Consultants and professional service providers.
Marketing activation partners and business representatives.
Other third parties engaged by IMS.
This SOP covers:

Third-party onboarding and registration.

narrative.text: Employees may bypass their supervisor if the concern involves the supervisor or if they are uncomfortable reporting through normal reporting lines.

blocks.text: IMS strictly prohibits retaliation against any individual who:

Reports a concern in good faith.
Participates in an investigation.
Provides evidence or witness statements.
Retaliation includes:

Termination.
Demotion.
Harassment.
Reduction in work assignments.
Threats or intimidation.
Negative treatment linked to reporting.
Any retaliation allegation shall be investigated as a serious violation of company policy.

body.text: The whistleblower should provide:

Description of the concern.
Date and location.
Individuals involved.
Supporting information or evidence.
Witness details (if known).
Anonymous reports shall be accepted when sufficient information is provided.
HR or the designated Compliance Representative shall review the report within 5 business days.
The review shall determine:

Whether the concern falls within the scope of this procedure.
Potential risks to employees, clients, or the company.
Whether immediate action is required.
Where required, a formal investigation shall be initiated.
The investigation may include:

Interviews.
Document reviews.
Review of payroll records.
Review of HR records.
Review of safety reports.
Review of electronic communications where permitted.
All investigations shall be conducted confidentially and impartially.
Following investigation, IMS may implement:

Disciplinary action.
Additional training.
Policy revisions.
Process improvements.
Corrective action plans.
Contract termination for suppliers or contractors.
Legal or regulatory notifications where necessary.

blocks.text: IMS shall maintain confidentiality throughout the reporting and investigation process.
Information shall only be disclosed to:

Authorized investigators.
HR personnel.
Management personnel involved in decision-making.
Legal or regulatory authorities where required.
The identity of the whistleblower shall be protected to the maximum extent possible.
Knowingly false, malicious, or intentionally misleading reports may result in disciplinary action.
However, no action shall be taken against an individual who reports a concern in good faith, even if the allegation is ultimately unsubstantiated.
IMS shall ensure:

All employees receive information regarding whistleblower reporting channels during onboarding.
Annual ethics and workplace conduct awareness training is conducted.
Contract workers are informed of available reporting mechanisms.
Managers receive training on handling complaints appropriately.

narrative.text: The HR Department or Compliance Representative shall maintain records of:

Number of concerns reported.
Nature of allegations.
Investigation status.
Corrective actions implemented.
Retaliation complaints.
A summary of whistleblower cases and trends shall be reviewed by management annually.

blocks.text: The following records shall be maintained:

Whistleblower Reports.
Investigation Records.
Interview Notes.
Corrective Action Plans.
Retaliation Investigation Records.
Training Records.
Management Review Records.
Records shall be retained for a minimum of 7 years and protected against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
